A full 1 kN proof cannot be the first test. In the frame calculation, an absent connection can send that force through the surrounding structure and produce 17.78 mm incremental displacement and 35.30 mrad rotation.

The introduced installed errors include ±6 N at the jack and ±32 N per other force channel, finite actuation error and observation-age limits. Both directions must pass independently. Perfect bias cancellation is not assumed.

The 350 N absent-path cap has a modeled complete-prefix bound of 10.70 mm and 17.21 mrad, fitting the immobilized service envelope.

The observation test executed 1,000 synthetic cases each for healthy, absent, unintended-shunt and one-cheek contacts. All healthy cases passed; all three represented faulty classes were rejected. Those are tests of the introduced measurement model, not measured false-acceptance probabilities.

A path crossing every sensor region could still imitate a healthy connection. The model retains that indistinguishable negative control. The physical response is a guarded, inspectable connection boundary and conservative replacement of ambiguous states—not a claim that local measurements identify arbitrary hidden force paths.
